transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Anderson, thank you for coming back to the room. I wanted to sit down with you and have a conversation about Leo's medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he alright? I noticed he seemed a bit more lethargic after the dose.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how that would be worrying. It is a very difficult thing to sit with when you feel something is off with your child.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some things that didn't go quite right with how the dose was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the process. I'm sorry for any confusion this has caused you, but the ward was incredibly busy when the order was placed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care how busy the ward was. I'm asking specifically what happened to my son's dosage. Did he get the wrong drug?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was more of a systemic complication in how the request was managed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I work in hospital administration, Doctor. Please don't tell me it was a systemic complication. Was the dose incorrect?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion regarding the calculations.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is incredibly vague. I need a clear answer. Was the dose too high?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? My son is sleepy and I don't know why. Did you give him too much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring him very closely now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding the question. I want the facts.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a heavy moment. I want to hold space for how you're feeling right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need space. I need an explanation. Did you estimate his weight instead of weighing him?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that things happened very quickly during the admission.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So the answer is yes. You guessed his weight and gave him a dose based on that guess.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a discrepancy in the records.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have not once told me what the error was. You are speaking in circles.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for the stress this is causing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are apologizing for my stress, not for the mistake. Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team was working under a lot of pressure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not asking about the team's pressure. I am asking who decided to bypass the scale.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a complicated process involving several people.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not complicated. It is a failure of safety protocol. My son received a dose above the safe threshold because someone didn't use a scale.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you are very angry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am beyond angry. I am terrified. What is the plan to fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are keeping an eye on him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. What are the specific clinical steps to counteract the overdose? What are the markers you are looking for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how he responds over the next few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is completely unacceptable. I want to see the attending physician and I want a written report of the incident.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly look into that for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will look into it? Or you will do it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see what the attending says when they do their rounds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When are the rounds?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Usually in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am staying here until I have a clear medical plan on paper.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a lot to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am processing it just fine. I am processing that my son was put at risk because of a "systemic complication" and the resident in charge cannot tell me what the actual error was.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry that you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't feel that way. I know that way. Which of the two of us is actually seeing the facts here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we are both calm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am calm. I am professional. I am waiting for a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll probably have an update for you later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later is not a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll check back in when I can.

H.justification: Resident shows defensive escalation and dismissiveness under pushback, eventually attempting to police the patient's emotional state ('I just want to make sure we are both calm').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'systemic complication' despite repeated direct questioning.

A.justification: Responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the process', 'the ward', and 'the team', and apologies are directed at the patient's feelings rather than the error.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand this is frustrating') and names emotions ('angry') but fails to engage with the patient's specific concerns or emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague responses ('we are keeping an eye on him', 'we'll just see', 'update for you later') with no concrete plan or timeline.
